hypotheses:
One development command, plumb evaluate simple|complex [--model haiku|sonnet] [--loop N], runs a benchmark of plumb: a cheap model works through a scripted sequence of owner requests in a fresh scratch repository where plumb is set up, using plumb's tools; a second cheap model plays the owner and answers the questions plumb raises from the task's hidden brief; the run is scored on hidden acceptance checks and on plumb's own trail (records, questions, gates, stale links, proofs); every issue the model finds with plumb goes to an issues file kept for later reliability work; with --loop, each issue becomes a debug case, plumb's debug workflow fixes it on a branch of its own, and the benchmark runs again, the owner asked only when a fix would change a requirement's meaning.
will: add plumb evaluate <simple|complex> with --model (haiku by default, sonnet too) and --rounds N (one fix round by default, 0 to only document)
will: run each task as a scripted sequence of owner requests in a scratch repository with plumb set up, through Claude Code's headless mode, one request per turn
will: let a scripted owner model answer the questions the agent puts to the owner, from the task's hidden brief
will: score each run on hidden acceptance checks and plumb's trail, print one line and write score.json
will: collect the issues the model files about plumb in the run's folder and in one accumulated file
will: after every run, turn each issue into a debug case, fix it through the debug workflow, merge the fix through the merge check and run the task once more, by itself
will: ship two hand-written tasks: a simple playable game (terminal tic-tac-toe) and a complex task (a command-line expense tracker with a rule change mid-way)
won't: use a public coding benchmark: they measure code, not plumb's loop
won't: ask the owner anything during a run except through the debug workflow's existing meaning question
won't: touch plumb's own records or code from the benchmarked session: the scratch repository is separate, and fixes go to debug's own branches
won't: call a model through the API directly: the benchmarked model must go through Claude Code so plumb's hooks and skills are exercised
records.premise:
/plumb:plumb intent I want a very cheap way to stress test plumb. I want Haiku to use plumb and develop a simple playable game. Or feel free to find a relevant benchmark. Actually there could be a rather complex task and one quite simple game. The idea is to be able from one plumb dev command like plumb evaluate simple or plumb evaluate complex to be able to run this benchmark test and see how much haiku or Sonnet is able to implement autonomously using plumb tools. when ever Haiku finds issue, it writes into a file that we can later re-use to improve reliability of plumb

Question: When plumb evaluate runs and the model finds an issue, should plumb act on it itself (fix it on a branch and run the benchmark again), or should it only write the issue to a file for you to use later?

You said on 2026-10-21: "when ever Haiku finds issue, it writes into a file that we can later re-use to improve reliability of plumb"
Options: Only write the issue to a file (Recommended) (Issues are kept in a file for later reuse. Nothing is fixed or rerun automatically. Recommended: You asked that issues be written to a file that you can later re-use, which describes keeping them for later rather than fixing them on the spot.); Fix each issue on a branch, then rerun (After each run, plumb fixes the issues on a branch and runs the benchmark again, up to a set number of rounds.)
Answer: Evaluate just documents the issues. but then debug is called to work on those issues, and ensure plumb compliant merge of the fixes. Of course it should come back to the user with question tool when fixing implies changing the intent 

Question: Should plumb evaluate limit each benchmark run to 3 owner exchanges, 25 agent turns and 20 minutes?

You said on 2026-10-21: "I want a very cheap way to stress test plumb."
Options: Set these limits (Recommended) (Each request and run stops at 3 owner exchanges, 25 agent turns or 20 minutes, whichever comes first. Recommended: You said you want a very cheap way to stress test plumb, so bounding each run's cost fits your words, but you did not name the numbers, so you should confirm them.); No limits (Runs go on until the scripted task ends, with no cap on turns, owner exchanges or time.)
Answer: No limits
